journey: A sibling Chromium tab performs the real local Identity 'Use a different account' credential login, consent and PKCE callback, replacing the host-only buyer cookie while the original account-wishlist tab stays mounted.
The first tab revalidates through the real Commerce buyer-session BFF; its held response proves the prior wishlist is hidden and no new wishlist read starts while identity is pending.
After release, the production Gateway worker and runner-owned Postgres fixture return an empty, unlinked wishlist for the replacement buyer; the prior buyer's product stays absent.
The owned suite's existing customer-profile, login, store-isolation, address, reset, support rollback and other consumer checks remain in the same 12-test run.

test_setup.next_dist_dir: unique ignored per-run directories for spawned test apps; existing developer .next directories were not used
test_setup.headless_focus: window focus lifecycle event dispatched after bringToFront because headless Chromium does not consistently emit OS focus transitions
test_setup.identity_dependencies: two temporary symlinks to already-present Tailwind packages were used because apps/platform/identity/node_modules was absent; removed after the run

cleanup.test_owned_next_processes: none remained after run; only previously running developer Next processes were present

limits: Synthetic identities and data in a runner-owned disposable Postgres database only.
This does not establish hosted adoption, buyer-role RLS policy, production account switching, or full Phase 2/eleven-phase acceptance.
The seven-day versus thirty-minute legacy-session lifetime choice and hosted telemetry/drain remain owner and operations gates.
